search_materials.description: Find materials by part of their name. Matching ignores case, spaces and hyphens, so "ferrite core e30" finds "Ferrite Core E-30" and "22swg wire" finds "22 SWG Copper Wire". Returns each material's name, unit, stock type (STANDING or PER_JOB), quantity on hand and minimum level. Use it before creating a material (to catch duplicates), to resolve what the user typed into an exact name, and before opening any form that needs a material. An empty query lists all active materials.

inputs.stockType: Optional filter: STANDING (kept in stock, has a minimum) or PER_JOB (bought for a job).
inputs.includeInactive: true to include deactivated materials. Default false.

get_material_balance.description: Current stock of one or more materials: quantity with unit, average rate, stock value, minimum level, and flags for negative stock and below-minimum. Use for "how much X do we have", before issuing, and to explain a shortage. Answer with the quantity and unit in one sentence; give rates and values to the owner only when relevant.

Use for "what happened to X", "what did I issue this week", and to find the movement the owner wants to reverse. Paginated.

create_material.description: Opens the form to add a new raw material. ALWAYS call search_materials first: if something similar exists ("Copper Wire 22 SWG" vs "22 SWG Copper Wire"), ask whether it's the same one before calling this — duplicate materials are the fastest way the stock goes wrong. A material has exactly one unit, used for buying and issuing, and the unit and stock type can never change later, so get them right. STANDING materials need a minimum level. Calling this opens the form for the user to check and submit; nothing is saved until they submit it. Pass everything you can work out and leave the rest for the form.

inputs.stockType: STANDING (kept in stock, needs a minimum) or PER_JOB (bought only for a job).
inputs.minimumLevel: Reorder level in the material's unit. Required for STANDING; leave empty for PER_JOB.
inputs.hsnCode: HSN code, if the user has it.

inputs.movementId: The movement, from get_movement_history. Ids come from earlier read-tool results; never show them to the user.

list_pending_approvals.description: OWNER ONLY. Purchase orders and counts waiting for him, each with what he needs to decide: amount, supplier or count, the job it's for, biggest differences, and how long it has waited.

list_notifications.description: The user's own notifications, unread first (approvals done, POs rejected, stock below minimum, rate jumps). Never anyone else's.

mark_notifications_read.description: Marks the user's own notifications as read. Done by the app when the person opens their notifications; not for you to call.

inputs.notificationIds: Which ones; leave out for all. Ids come from earlier read-tool results; never show them to the user.

list_reorder_alerts.description: STANDING materials below their minimum level: on hand, minimum and shortfall, with units. Offer a purchase order for the shortfall (rate empty).

get_stock_value.description: OWNER ONLY. Total stock value and value per material at average rates (quantity times average rate). Name materials to get only those, e.g. "value of copper wire in stock".

inputs.materialNames: Only these materials. Material names as returned by search_materials, e.g. ["22 SWG Copper Wire"].

estimate_job_cost.description: OWNER ONLY. What-if: the material cost of the jobs not yet closed at today's average rates, against the same with one material's rate changed — e.g. copper at ₹900/kg. Same costing as the job cost report. Nothing is saved and no price changes anywhere. Use it for "what if copper goes to…" questions and in what-if artifacts. Never do the sums yourself.

inputs.jobIds: Only these jobs; leave out for all open jobs. Ids come from earlier read-tool results; never show them to the user.
inputs.materialNames: The material whose rate changes. Material names as returned by search_materials, e.g. ["22 SWG Copper Wire"].
inputs.newRate: The rate to try, in ₹ per unit. This is a what-if input, not a price.

get_job_cost_report.description: OWNER ONLY. Material cost per job: pieces, cost (value issued less value returned) and cost per piece. By default the jobs closed in the period; set includeOpen for open jobs too (their cost so far), which is also how to see every job under one customer PO, each costed separately.

inputs.from: From (closed on or after; job date when includeOpen). Date as YYYY-MM-DD (Asia/Kolkata), or @today, @today-7d (days back), or @month (the first of this month).
inputs.to: To. Date as YYYY-MM-DD (Asia/Kolkata), or @today, @today-7d (days back), or @month (the first of this month).
inputs.customerId: One customer. Ids come from earlier read-tool results; never show them to the user.
inputs.customerPoId: Only jobs under this customer PO, from list_customer_pos. Ids come from earlier read-tool results; never show them to the user.
inputs.includeOpen: true to include jobs that are not closed yet.

get_activity.description: OWNER ONLY. Who did what and when, newest first, and whether it was done through the chat assistant, a form, a button or an artifact. Filter by person, kind of action, date or one job (every change to that job). Use it for "everything the agent did today" (from @today) and "all changes to job 31".

inputs.userId: One person. Ids come from earlier read-tool results; never show them to the user.
inputs.from: From. Date as YYYY-MM-DD (Asia/Kolkata), or @today, @today-7d (days back), or @month (the first of this month).
inputs.to: To. Date as YYYY-MM-DD (Asia/Kolkata), or @today, @today-7d (days back), or @month (the first of this month).
inputs.tool: One kind of action, e.g. issue_material.
inputs.jobId: Only changes to this job. Ids come from earlier read-tool results; never show them to the user.

reset_demo_data.description: OWNER ONLY, demo copy only. Opens the form to wipe the demo stock, jobs, orders and history and fill in a fresh demo month. Logins and settings stay. Use it only when the owner asks to start the demo again; say it cannot be undone. On a real copy it refuses. Calling this opens the form for the user to check and submit; nothing is saved until they submit it. Pass everything you can work out and leave the rest for the form.

inputs.confirm: Leave empty: the owner ticks the box on the form.

get_print_data.description: Used by the app to fill the five printouts. Never called by the assistant.

list_settings.description: Settings. The owner sees all of them; the storekeeper sees only the purchase approval limit.

update_setting.description: OWNER ONLY. Opens the form to change a setting such as the purchase approval limit. If the storekeeper asks, say only the owner changes it. Calling this opens the form for the user to check and submit; nothing is saved until they submit it. Pass everything you can work out and leave the rest for the form.

inputs.value: The new value, e.g. 50000 for a ₹50,000 approval limit.

list_users.description: OWNER ONLY. People who can log in: name, role, active. Never passwords.

create_user.description: OWNER ONLY. Opens the form to add a login. The owner types the initial password in the form; never put a password in the chat or in this call. Calling this opens the form for the user to check and submit; nothing is saved until they submit it. Pass everything you can work out and leave the rest for the form.

reset_user_password.description: OWNER ONLY. Opens the form to set a new password for someone who forgot theirs. The owner types the new password in the form; never put a password in the chat or in this call. Calling this opens the form for the user to check and submit; nothing is saved until they submit it. Pass everything you can work out and leave the rest for the form.

inputs.userId: The person. Ids come from earlier read-tool results; never show them to the user.

deactivate_user.description: OWNER ONLY. Opens the form to stop a person logging in. The last active owner can't be deactivated. Calling this opens the form for the user to check and submit; nothing is saved until they submit it. Pass everything you can work out and leave the rest for the form.

inputs.userId: The person. Ids come from earlier read-tool results; never show them to the user.

list_artifacts.description: The user's saved and recent artifacts and, for the storekeeper, the ones the owner shared with him. ALWAYS call this before make_artifact when someone asks for a report, chart or dashboard: if one already does the job, open it with open_artifact and say so instead of building a duplicate.

inputs.query: Words from the title or what it shows, e.g. "copper" or "below minimum".

open_artifact.description: Opens a saved, recent or shared artifact beside the chat. It runs again with live numbers when opened.

inputs.artifactId: The artifact's id from list_artifacts or the panel. Ids come from earlier read-tool results; never show them to the user.

make_artifact.description: Builds an artifact that opens beside the chat with live numbers. ONLY when the user asks for a report, memo, SOP, diagram, chart, dashboard, comparison, what-if or a long list (more than ~10 rows or 5 columns). NOT for a single fact (say it), a short list (show a table in the chat), a change of data (open the form), or the fixed printouts (open_printout). Two kinds: a document (reports, memos, SOPs, flow diagrams, explainers; downloads as PDF, Word, Excel, CSV, picture or Markdown) and a page (an interactive what-if or filters). Leave kind out and the builder chooses. It can only look and point: it reads data and can open a form, never save. Never put figures you worked out into the request; the numbers come from the system. Returns the title, a one-line summary and anything it couldn't include.

inputs.request: What the artifact is for, in plain words, including any period, materials, jobs or suppliers, and any buttons wanted (e.g. "Materials below minimum with a Make PO button on each row"). Do not include numbers you calculated.
inputs.kind: Optional: document or page. document for something to read, print or send (report, memo, SOP, diagram); page only if the user will interact with it (what-if, filters). Leave out to let the builder choose.

edit_artifact.description: Changes an artifact the user made, a document or a page — "make it a bar chart", "add a supplier column", "add a step to the flow". It becomes a new version at once and earlier versions can be restored. A copy the owner shared with the storekeeper does not change. Never make a new artifact for a change to an existing one.

inputs.artifactId: The artifact's id from the panel or list_artifacts. Default: the one open beside the chat.
inputs.request: The change, in the user's words plus anything you worked out. No calculated numbers.

open_printout.description: Opens a printable document with the Vijaya letterhead, ready to print or save as PDF: purchase-order (to send the supplier; only approved POs print without a "not approved" mark), goods-receipt-note, issue-slip (the pick list for a job; printing issues nothing), count-sheet (with an empty Counted column) and job-cost-sheet (owner only). These are the only printouts. There is no tax invoice, delivery challan or quotation: say invoicing and dispatch aren't set up.

inputs.template: purchase-order, goods-receipt-note, issue-slip, count-sheet or job-cost-sheet.
inputs.with: What to print: {"purchaseOrder": id} | {"receipt": id} | {"job": id} | {"count": id}. Ids come from earlier read-tool results; never show them to the user.

share_artifact.description: OWNER ONLY. Opens the form to share one frozen version of an artifact with the storekeeper. His copy does not change until the owner shares a newer version. Refused if the artifact uses owner-only data (stock value total, leak, job cost, scrap, activity): say which part and offer a version without it. Calling this opens the form for the user to check and submit; nothing is saved until they submit it. Pass everything you can work out and leave the rest for the form.

inputs.artifactId: The artifact. Ids come from earlier read-tool results; never show them to the user.
inputs.version: Optional: the version number to share. Default: the current one.

unshare_artifact.description: OWNER ONLY. Opens the form to stop sharing an artifact with the storekeeper; it disappears from his Saved. Calling this opens the form for the user to check and submit; nothing is saved until they submit it. Pass everything you can work out and leave the rest for the form.

inputs.artifactId: The artifact. Ids come from earlier read-tool results; never show them to the user.

download_data.description: Makes a file to download. Use it when the user says "as PDF", "in Word", "in Excel", "as CSV", "as a picture", "as Markdown", "send me this", "for the accountant". Give the format the user named. A document artifact can be pdf, docx, xlsx, csv, png or md; a page artifact pdf, png, xlsx or csv; a table in the chat xlsx or csv. The file is made by the server with the user's own role, so it never includes anything they can't see. The system can't email or send it: the user downloads it and sends it himself. For the letterhead printouts (purchase order and so on) use open_printout instead.

inputs.format: pdf, docx, xlsx, csv, png or md. Must be one this kind of artifact has (see above).
inputs.source: For a table: {"tool": a read tool, "input": {...}}, the same as you'd call it.
inputs.artifactId: Or an artifact: its id, to download it. Default: the one open beside the chat.
inputs.title: File name in plain words, e.g. "Copper receipts". The date is added.
